topics.objective: Select, maintain and use basketry tools safely for measuring, cutting, piercing, shaping and colouring operations.

questions.prompt: Which attribute makes well-conditioned cane suitable for forming a curved basket handle?

options.label: A
options.text: It bends with useful toughness without splitting
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. A handle needs a material that can follow a controlled curve while retaining tensile strength, so conditioned cane is selected for flexibility and toughness rather than complete rigidity.

options.label: B
options.text: It is highly rigid and should remain straight under normal forming loads
options.rationale: A handle must be formed into a curve, so complete rigidity would prevent the required shaping rather than make the cane suitable.

options.label: C
options.text: It has useful bulk but cannot follow a controlled curve without fracturing
options.rationale: Bulk without bending capacity describes an unsuitable handle material because the member would crack before reaching the planned radius.

options.label: D
options.text: It stays excessively soft after soaking and recovers little structural stiffness
options.rationale: Conditioning is temporary; sound cane regains useful stiffness after drying instead of remaining permanently soft and unable to carry load.

questions.workedSolution: A handle needs a material that can follow a controlled curve while retaining tensile strength, so conditioned cane is selected for flexibility and toughness rather than complete rigidity. Therefore the correct answer is A: It bends with useful toughness without splitting.

questions.prompt: Which statement describes a material attribute rather than a use of that material?

options.label: A
options.text: Raffia is selected to wrap a coiled basket core
options.rationale: Wrapping a core identifies an application chosen for the material; it does not state an inherent quality such as flexibility or width.

options.label: B
options.text: Raffia is woven into the decorative band of a table mat
options.rationale: A decorative band is a product use, whereas an attribute must describe how the raffia itself behaves or can be measured.

options.label: C
options.text: A raffia strip is soft and flexible when properly conditioned
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Softness and flexibility are inherent working qualities that can be observed or tested; the other statements name applications and therefore describe uses rather than attributes.

options.label: D
options.text: Raffia is tied around the finished rim of a lightweight tray
options.rationale: Rim tying describes where the fibre is employed in construction, not a physical or working property of the raffia strip.

questions.workedSolution: Softness and flexibility are inherent working qualities that can be observed or tested; the other statements name applications and therefore describe uses rather than attributes. Therefore the correct answer is C: A raffia strip is soft and flexible when properly conditioned.

questions.prompt: Why are properly prepared corn shucks suitable for plaited or wrapped basketry details?

options.label: A
options.text: Their untreated dry fibres bend repeatedly without conditioning or cracking
options.rationale: Dry shucks can become brittle; controlled moistening is normally required before close folds or repeated bending.

options.label: B
options.text: Their woody circular section carries the main load of a rigid basket frame
options.rationale: Corn shucks are broad leaf material rather than woody rods, so they suit wrapping and plaiting more than a primary rigid frame.

options.label: C
options.text: Their broad fibres become pliable when conditioned and can be folded closely
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Conditioned corn shucks provide broad flexible strips for folding, plaiting and wrapping, but they are not a substitute for sound cane where the design requires a stiff structural framework.

options.label: D
options.text: Their short cross-grain structure gives greater rim strength than mature cane
options.rationale: Their value is pliable surface coverage, not greater structural rim strength than sound long-fibred cane.

questions.workedSolution: Conditioned corn shucks provide broad flexible strips for folding, plaiting and wrapping, but they are not a substitute for sound cane where the design requires a stiff structural framework. Therefore the correct answer is C: Their broad fibres become pliable when conditioned and can be folded closely.

questions.prompt: Which quality makes prepared date-palm leaflets useful for light plaited basketry?

options.label: A
options.text: They split into long flexible strips that interlace with regular spacing
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Sound date-palm leaflets can be dried, split and reconditioned into long strips whose lengthwise fibres support plaiting and light containers when thickness and defects are controlled.

options.label: B
options.text: They form a dense round rod intended mainly for heavy structural stakes
options.rationale: Prepared leaflets are split flat material for lighter interlacing, not naturally dense round rods for a heavy stake framework.

options.label: C
options.text: They normally remain ready to weave after long dry storage without reconditioning
options.rationale: Palm strips dry during storage and may need reconditioning; they do not retain permanent working moisture.

options.label: D
options.text: Their crosswise strength is the main reason they can be split into long strips
options.rationale: Their longitudinal fibres are precisely what support useful strip length, so strength is not equal across and along the leaflet.

questions.workedSolution: Sound date-palm leaflets can be dried, split and reconditioned into long strips whose lengthwise fibres support plaiting and light containers when thickness and defects are controlled. Therefore the correct answer is A: They split into long flexible strips that interlace with regular spacing.

questions.prompt: Which material condition should cause a craftsperson to reject a cane intended for a load-bearing rim?

options.label: A
options.text: A shallow surface stain that can be cleaned without fibre loss
options.rationale: A removable superficial stain may affect appearance but does not necessarily weaken the continuous fibres of a load-bearing rim.

options.label: B
options.text: A consistent colour variation that does not interrupt the cane fibres
options.rationale: Colour variation alone is not structural damage when the fibres remain continuous, sound and appropriate for the intended finish.

options.label: C
options.text: A gradual natural taper that can be allowed for during sizing
options.rationale: Moderate taper is common in natural cane and can be graded or positioned without requiring rejection of an otherwise sound length.

options.label: D
options.text: Deep insect channels that interrupt the fibres
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. A load-bearing rim depends on continuous sound fibres, and deep insect damage reduces its section and strength even when the cane can still be bent into the required outline.

questions.workedSolution: A load-bearing rim depends on continuous sound fibres, and deep insect damage reduces its section and strength even when the cane can still be bent into the required outline. Therefore the correct answer is D: Deep insect channels that interrupt the fibres.

questions.prompt: What should guide the selection of cane during responsible harvesting for basketry?

options.label: A
options.text: Cut stems to one market diameter across each clump and rely on the rootstock for uniform regrowth
options.rationale: Diameter-based clearance removes mixed-age replacement growth; selective cutting should retain younger stems and the clump's regenerative structure.

options.label: B
options.text: Choose mature sound stems and leave immature growth to develop
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Mature sound stems provide stronger usable fibres, while leaving young growth and regenerative parts supports both future material quality and continued production from the resource.

options.label: C
options.text: Prefer the oldest thick stems even when shallow checks are visible along their length
options.rationale: Greater diameter does not compensate for checks that interrupt fibre continuity and can open further during preparation, bending or drying.

options.label: D
options.text: Harvest the softest immature shoots and retain the mature stems for later seasons
options.rationale: Immature shoots are still developing their fibres and dimensions, so reversing the age selection reduces both present quality and future regeneration.

questions.workedSolution: Mature sound stems provide stronger usable fibres, while leaving young growth and regenerative parts supports both future material quality and continued production from the resource. Therefore the correct answer is B: Choose mature sound stems and leave immature growth to develop.

questions.prompt: Why is dry cane soaked or damp-conditioned before it is bent sharply?

options.label: A
options.text: Soaking closes insect channels enough to restore a damaged structural length
options.rationale: Moisture can improve temporary workability but cannot reconstruct fibres already removed or weakened by insects.

options.label: B
options.text: Water raises the natural tensile strength beyond that of sound unsoaked cane
options.rationale: The purpose is safer bending, not creation of strength beyond the capacity of the original sound material.

options.label: C
options.text: Conditioning makes cane water-resistant enough to need no later protection
options.rationale: Conditioning does not waterproof cane; protection from later moisture still depends on drying, design and an appropriate finish.

options.label: D
options.text: Moisture restores temporary pliability and reduces surface splitting
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Controlled conditioning lets fibres move relative to one another during forming, reducing cracking; it does not repair decay or make an unsuitable bend radius automatically safe.

questions.workedSolution: Controlled conditioning lets fibres move relative to one another during forming, reducing cracking; it does not repair decay or make an unsuitable bend radius automatically safe. Therefore the correct answer is D: Moisture restores temporary pliability and reduces surface splitting.

questions.prompt: What is the main reason for sizing weaving strips to a consistent width and thickness?

options.label: A
options.text: Alternate wider and narrower strips by eye while applying the same pull throughout each course
options.rationale: Unmeasured width changes alter coverage even under equal pull, making course spacing and the intended shape difficult to reproduce consistently.

options.label: B
options.text: Size flexible weavers to the same gauge as the stakes so one dimension serves both structural roles
options.rationale: Stakes and weavers perform different functions and may require different gauges; making them identical does not create uniform woven response.

options.label: C
options.text: Uniform strips support even tension, spacing and appearance
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Consistent preparation makes the strips respond similarly during bending and tightening, helping the maker maintain regular courses without local bulges, gaps or weak narrow sections.

options.label: D
options.text: Grade strips to one width but allow thickness to vary so thicker sections reinforce tight bends
options.rationale: Thickness variation changes bending resistance, so a strip that thickens at a tight curve is more likely to disturb spacing or force than reinforce it predictably.

questions.workedSolution: Consistent preparation makes the strips respond similarly during bending and tightening, helping the maker maintain regular courses without local bulges, gaps or weak narrow sections. Therefore the correct answer is C: Uniform strips support even tension, spacing and appearance.

questions.prompt: Which sequence best controls chemical colouring of prepared bamboo strips?

options.label: A
options.text: Place partly dry and fully damp sized strips together in a measured bath, then rinse and dry them at one time
options.rationale: Different starting moisture conditions alter absorption rates, causing uneven uptake even when bath strength and final removal time are controlled.

options.label: B
options.text: Prepare a measured bath, add strips in several timed batches, remove them together, then rinse and dry
options.rationale: A common removal time gives later batches shorter exposure than earlier ones, so measured concentration alone cannot produce repeatable matching colour.

options.label: C
options.text: Clean and size the strips, prepare a measured bath, immerse for a controlled time, rinse or neutralise as directed, then dry
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Controlled chemical colouring begins with uniformly prepared bamboo and a measured compatible bath, followed by equal exposure, the specified rinse or neutralisation, and thorough drying for repeatable colour and safer handling.

options.label: D
options.text: Clean broad strips, colour them before final sizing, shave them to width, then dry without a final rinse
options.rationale: Sizing after colouring exposes fresh lighter edges and changes strip dimensions, while omitting the directed rinse can leave reactive residue behind.

questions.workedSolution: Controlled chemical colouring begins with uniformly prepared bamboo and a measured compatible bath, followed by equal exposure, the specified rinse or neutralisation, and thorough drying for repeatable colour and safer handling. Therefore the correct answer is C: Clean and size the strips, prepare a measured bath, immerse for a controlled time, rinse or neutralise as directed, then dry.

questions.prompt: How should prepared basketry materials be stored before use?

options.label: A
options.text: Raised in a dry ventilated place and protected from pests
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Dry ventilated storage limits mould, staining and pest activity while preserving material condition; wet sealed bundles create a favourable environment for biological deterioration.

options.label: B
options.text: Stack dry strips directly on a concrete floor under an open cover because the room is ventilated
options.rationale: Concrete can transfer ground moisture and harbour pests, so ventilation above the stack does not replace raised, isolated storage.

options.label: C
options.text: Tie all graded strips into dense bundles and inspect them only when they are issued for weaving
options.rationale: Dense unmonitored bundles restrict air movement and conceal early pest or moisture problems that routine inspection should detect.

options.label: D
options.text: Keep freshly conditioned strips sealed in plastic sacks in a warm room for several days to preserve flexibility
options.rationale: Several days of warm sealed storage trap moisture with little air exchange, encouraging mould, staining and odour; short controlled conditioning should not be treated as long-term storage.

questions.workedSolution: Dry ventilated storage limits mould, staining and pest activity while preserving material condition; wet sealed bundles create a favourable environment for biological deterioration. Therefore the correct answer is A: Raised in a dry ventilated place and protected from pests.

questions.prompt: What is the safest method for trimming a tough cane strip with a knife?

options.label: A
options.text: Hold the strip unsupported so it can move away from a heavy stroke
options.rationale: Unsupported material twists and changes the cutting angle, reducing control and increasing the chance of a glancing cut.

options.label: B
options.text: Use a blunt knife with greater force because it is less likely to cut skin
options.rationale: A blunt edge demands excess force and is more likely to skid; sharpness must be combined with safe direction and workholding.

options.label: C
options.text: Brace the strip against the palm and cut toward the supporting hand
options.rationale: Cutting toward the supporting hand places it directly in the blade path if the edge slips or passes through the strip.

options.label: D
options.text: Secure the material and cut away from the body with a controlled stroke
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Securing the work and directing a sharp blade away from the body improves control and keeps hands outside the cutting path, reducing slips caused by unstable material or excessive force.

questions.workedSolution: Securing the work and directing a sharp blade away from the body improves control and keeps hands outside the cutting path, reducing slips caused by unstable material or excessive force. Therefore the correct answer is D: Secure the material and cut away from the body with a controlled stroke.

questions.prompt: Which description identifies a Josephine knot in decorative basketry or cord work?

options.label: A
options.text: A folded cord passes around a support to form a lark’s-head attachment
options.rationale: A lark’s head attaches a folded cord to a support and has a different load path and appearance from a Josephine knot.

options.label: B
options.text: Two interlaced bights form a flat symmetrical decorative knot
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. The Josephine knot is recognised by its balanced interlaced loops and flat decorative form; the alternatives describe other useful knots but not its distinctive structure.

options.label: C
options.text: A working cord makes successive half hitches along one holding cord
options.rationale: Repeated half hitches can form a macrame bar or spiral, but they do not produce the Josephine knot’s flat symmetric loops.

options.label: D
options.text: Two cord ends cross once and tighten into a compact overhand stopper
options.rationale: A single crossing tightened as a stopper describes an overhand knot, not the paired interlaced bights of a Josephine knot.

questions.workedSolution: The Josephine knot is recognised by its balanced interlaced loops and flat decorative form; the alternatives describe other useful knots but not its distinctive structure. Therefore the correct answer is B: Two interlaced bights form a flat symmetrical decorative knot.

questions.prompt: Which procedure forms a simple overhand knot?

options.label: A
options.text: Wrap a working strand around a core and stitch each turn to the preceding one
options.rationale: Wrapping and stitching a core is a coiling construction sequence and does not describe the formation of an overhand knot.

options.label: B
options.text: Fold a cord into a bight and pull both ends through it around a support
options.rationale: Passing both ends through a folded bight around a support creates a lark’s-head attachment, not a single-cord overhand knot.

options.label: C
options.text: Cross two separate cord ends twice in opposite directions to make a square knot
options.rationale: Opposed crossings of two ends describe a square knot, which joins or binds two parts rather than forming one overhand knot.

options.label: D
options.text: Make a loop in one cord, pass the working end through it once, and tighten
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. An overhand knot is the basic single-cord knot formed by passing the working end through its own loop; the other procedures create a square knot, lark’s head or wrapped coil.

questions.workedSolution: An overhand knot is the basic single-cord knot formed by passing the working end through its own loop; the other procedures create a square knot, lark’s head or wrapped coil. Therefore the correct answer is D: Make a loop in one cord, pass the working end through it once, and tighten.

questions.prompt: What structure is produced by a square-knot sinnet in macrame?

options.label: A
options.text: A flat band of complete square knots repeated in sequence on the same cord group
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. A sinnet is a chain of repeated knots. Repeating complete square knots, each formed from opposing half-knots, produces a relatively flat band suitable for a basket handle or decorative structural strip.

options.label: B
options.text: A mounting row made by attaching folded cords to a support with lark's-head knots
options.rationale: Lark's-head knots mount folded cords onto a support and form an attachment row, not the repeated flat chain specified by a square-knot sinnet.

options.label: C
options.text: A ribbed line made by working double half hitches successively along a carrier cord
options.rationale: Successive double half hitches create a hitch line along a holding cord; they do not repeat complete square knots on one cord group.

options.label: D
options.text: A spiral column made by repeating the same half-knot direction around filler cords
options.rationale: Repeated half-knots begun from the same side rotate around the filler cords and form a spiral rather than a flat square-knot sinnet.

questions.workedSolution: A sinnet is a chain of repeated knots. Repeating complete square knots, each formed from opposing half-knots, produces a relatively flat band suitable for a basket handle or decorative structural strip. Therefore the correct answer is A: A flat band of complete square knots repeated in sequence on the same cord group.

questions.prompt: Which control is appropriate when mixing or applying a basketry dye?

options.label: A
options.text: Use suitable gloves, ventilation and the dye manufacturer’s handling guidance
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Dyes and auxiliaries may irritate skin or release vapour, so labelled containers, ventilation, protective equipment and product-specific instructions reduce exposure and contamination risks.

options.label: B
options.text: Rely on an open window alone without checking the dye handling instructions
options.rationale: General ventilation may be insufficient for a particular dye or auxiliary; product guidance determines the required controls.

options.label: C
options.text: Decant leftover dye into an unlabelled drink bottle for later use
options.rationale: A drink container invites mistaken ingestion and loses hazard information, so dye must remain in a compatible labelled vessel.

options.label: D
options.text: Increase concentration beyond guidance so gloves and ventilation are needed for less time
options.rationale: Excess concentration can increase exposure, fibre damage and colour variation rather than making an unsafe process acceptably shorter.

questions.workedSolution: Dyes and auxiliaries may irritate skin or release vapour, so labelled containers, ventilation, protective equipment and product-specific instructions reduce exposure and contamination risks. Therefore the correct answer is A: Use suitable gloves, ventilation and the dye manufacturer’s handling guidance.

questions.prompt: In stake-and-strand basketry, what is the structural role of the stakes?

options.label: A
options.text: They serve as temporary spacers and are removed when the sides are firm
options.rationale: Stakes remain integrated in the base, walls and border because removing them would destroy the supporting framework.

options.label: B
options.text: They form the supporting framework around which the weavers pass
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Stakes establish the form and resist loads along the basket wall, while more flexible strands travel around them to bind the framework into a continuous surface.

options.label: C
options.text: They are the flexible strands that complete the horizontal courses
options.rationale: The moving horizontal elements are weavers; stakes are the more stable uprights around which those strands travel.

options.label: D
options.text: They are decorative rim ends added only after the basket is complete
options.rationale: Although stake ends may enter a decorative border, their structural role begins before the rim and continues through the body.

questions.workedSolution: Stakes establish the form and resist loads along the basket wall, while more flexible strands travel around them to bind the framework into a continuous surface. Therefore the correct answer is B: They form the supporting framework around which the weavers pass.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes pairing or twining from simple one-strand randing?

options.label: A
options.text: Two weavers cross around successive stakes as the course advances
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Pairing uses two active strands that exchange position around the uprights, producing a locking course that can strengthen starts, borders and changes in the basket form.

options.label: B
options.text: One strand passes alternately over and under successive stakes
options.rationale: A single alternating strand describes simple randing; pairing requires two active weavers exchanging position.

options.label: C
options.text: A bundled core is wrapped and stitched to the preceding round
options.rationale: A stitched bundled core is coiled basketry and does not use two weavers crossing around a stake framework.

options.label: D
options.text: Broad strips cross diagonally without twisting around upright stakes
options.rationale: Diagonal strip interlacing describes plaiting, whereas pairing locks two strands around successive uprights.

questions.workedSolution: Pairing uses two active strands that exchange position around the uprights, producing a locking course that can strengthen starts, borders and changes in the basket form. Therefore the correct answer is A: Two weavers cross around successive stakes as the course advances.

questions.prompt: Why is an odd number of stakes useful for continuous over-one-under-one randing?

options.label: A
options.text: An even stake count normally shifts the sequence after each continuous round
options.rationale: With an even count, a continuous over-one-under-one weaver returns to the same relationship unless the sequence is deliberately changed.

options.label: B
options.text: Removing a stake at the end of a round is the normal way to maintain alternation
options.rationale: Regularly removing stakes would alter spacing and weaken the framework; the odd count provides the shift without that damage.

options.label: C
options.text: Successive rounds reverse the over-under relationship at each stake
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. With an odd stake count, returning to the starting area shifts the sequence, so the next round alternates correctly instead of stacking identical crossings above one another.

options.label: D
options.text: Stake number matters only to rim decoration and not continuous randing
options.rationale: Stake parity affects where the continuous strand meets each upright throughout the body, not only at the border.

questions.workedSolution: With an odd stake count, returning to the starting area shifts the sequence, so the next round alternates correctly instead of stacking identical crossings above one another. Therefore the correct answer is C: Successive rounds reverse the over-under relationship at each stake.

questions.prompt: What is the likely effect of pulling one side’s weavers much tighter than the other side’s?

options.label: A
options.text: The basket form will distort toward the tighter area
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Unequal tension changes spacing and bends the stakes asymmetrically, so regular checking and gradual correction are needed to maintain the intended diameter, profile and alignment.

options.label: B
options.text: A strong round border can correct accumulated wall distortion at the finishing stage
options.rationale: A rim cannot reliably undo accumulated wall distortion and may introduce new stress if the underlying courses remain unequal.

options.label: C
options.text: Unequal tension changes gaps but has little influence on the basket profile
options.rationale: Spacing and shape are linked because tight strands pull the supporting stakes and can narrow or lean the body locally.

options.label: D
options.text: The tighter side expands farther because tension pushes its stakes outward
options.rationale: Higher tension normally draws elements inward rather than expanding that side farther from the centre.

questions.workedSolution: Unequal tension changes spacing and bends the stakes asymmetrically, so regular checking and gradual correction are needed to maintain the intended diameter, profile and alignment. Therefore the correct answer is A: The basket form will distort toward the tighter area.

questions.prompt: What form develops when half-knots are repeated from the same side in macrame?

options.label: A
options.text: The knots align as a straight row of double half hitches along a separate carrier cord
options.rationale: Double half hitches are tied to a holding or carrier cord and form a line, which is structurally different from a half-knot spiral around fillers.

options.label: B
options.text: The working cords rotate around the fillers to form a spiral sinnet
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. A half-knot is one side of a square knot. Repeating that same side makes the working cords advance around the filler cords, creating the characteristic twisted or spiral sinnet instead of a flat square-knot band.

options.label: C
options.text: The repeated half-knots secure folded cords to a support in the same pattern as lark's-head mounting
options.rationale: Lark's-head attachments require folded cords placed around a support; repeated half-knots do not mount the cord group in that way.

options.label: D
options.text: The alternating halves settle into a flat square-knot sinnet without directional twist
options.rationale: A flat square-knot sinnet requires opposing half-knots to alternate; repeating one side preserves the rotational bias and produces a spiral.

questions.workedSolution: A half-knot is one side of a square knot. Repeating that same side makes the working cords advance around the filler cords, creating the characteristic twisted or spiral sinnet instead of a flat square-knot band. Therefore the correct answer is B: The working cords rotate around the fillers to form a spiral sinnet.

questions.prompt: How is visual balance achieved in an asymmetrical basket decoration?

options.label: A
options.text: Give the shapes similar size and colour without considering visual weight
options.rationale: Equal dimensions do not guarantee equal visual weight because colour, texture, position and shape affect emphasis differently.

options.label: B
options.text: Use mirrored motifs because asymmetrical layouts usually lack balance
options.rationale: Symmetry is one route to balance, but unequal elements can also be distributed to create stable visual weight.

options.label: C
options.text: Different elements are arranged so their visual weights feel stable without mirroring
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Asymmetrical balance can combine unequal shapes, colours or textures while distributing their visual emphasis so the finished composition still feels stable and intentional.

options.label: D
options.text: Place the largest dark motif at one edge without a countering element
options.rationale: A dominant edge element requires an intentional counterweight or spacing response; isolation alone usually makes the design feel unstable.

questions.workedSolution: Asymmetrical balance can combine unequal shapes, colours or textures while distributing their visual emphasis so the finished composition still feels stable and intentional. Therefore the correct answer is C: Different elements are arranged so their visual weights feel stable without mirroring.

questions.prompt: What design effect is produced by repeating a coloured weaving unit at regular intervals?

options.label: A
options.text: Harmony created by using closely related colours without a repeated interval
options.rationale: Related colours may create harmony, but rhythm specifically depends on recurrence or progression that moves the eye.

options.label: B
options.text: Proportion created by changing the handle size relative to the body
options.rationale: Handle-to-body size is a proportion decision, whereas rhythm arises from repeated units, spacing or directional change.

options.label: C
options.text: Rhythm that guides the eye around the form
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Regular repetition establishes an expected visual beat, and carefully varied spacing or colour can strengthen movement without undermining the functional woven structure.

options.label: D
options.text: Emphasis created by one isolated contrasting motif at the centre
options.rationale: One isolated contrast establishes emphasis or a focal point; it does not provide the repeated visual beat described in the question.

questions.workedSolution: Regular repetition establishes an expected visual beat, and carefully varied spacing or colour can strengthen movement without undermining the functional woven structure. Therefore the correct answer is C: Rhythm that guides the eye around the form.

questions.prompt: Why should the scale of a handle be considered in relation to the basket body?

options.label: A
options.text: Use one standard handle dimension for baskets with different carrying purposes
options.rationale: Body size, contents and hand clearance vary, so a single standard dimension cannot provide suitable proportion and function in every design.

options.label: B
options.text: Choose the shortest handle because reduced span is the main capacity requirement
options.rationale: Shortness alone does not establish capacity; an undersized grip can be uncomfortable and its attachment may concentrate load.

options.label: C
options.text: Judge the handle only by colour because scale does not affect grip
options.rationale: Colour contributes visually, but handle dimensions determine clearance, leverage, comfort and its relationship to the basket mass.

options.label: D
options.text: Proportion affects both visual unity and comfortable functional use
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. A handle that relates to the body’s size and load appears integrated and provides suitable clearance and grip; poor proportion can impair both appearance and usability.

questions.workedSolution: A handle that relates to the body’s size and load appears integrated and provides suitable clearance and grip; poor proportion can impair both appearance and usability. Therefore the correct answer is D: Proportion affects both visual unity and comfortable functional use.

questions.prompt: Which colour decision is most likely to produce a controlled harmonious pattern?

options.label: A
options.text: Choose each colour after its strip is woven so no full scheme is considered
options.rationale: Postponing every choice prevents control of repeats and relationships across the complete form.

options.label: B
options.text: Select a limited related palette and repeat it according to a plan
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. A planned limited palette lets natural and dyed materials relate coherently, while deliberate repetition makes colour changes readable as part of the design rather than accidental repairs.

options.label: C
options.text: Combine different dye batches without sampling because their labels match
options.rationale: Natural fibres and dye batches can vary, so a sample is needed before assuming labelled colours will match in the finished pattern.

options.label: D
options.text: Use many high-intensity colours in equal amounts to create harmony
options.rationale: Equal areas of many intense colours can compete strongly; harmony depends on planned relationships and proportions, not quantity alone.

questions.workedSolution: A planned limited palette lets natural and dyed materials relate coherently, while deliberate repetition makes colour changes readable as part of the design rather than accidental repairs. Therefore the correct answer is B: Select a limited related palette and repeat it according to a plan.

questions.prompt: Why should a prototype be made before producing a new basket design in quantity?

options.label: A
options.text: It mainly serves as a colour sample and may omit the proposed construction
options.rationale: A colour-only sample cannot test dimensions, strength, ergonomics or the construction sequence of the intended product.

options.label: B
options.text: It fixes the price without recording material, labour or overhead
options.rationale: A prototype can reveal quantities and time, but a price still requires recorded costs and a reasoned margin.

options.label: C
options.text: It tests dimensions, construction, appearance and fitness for purpose before repeated production
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. A prototype combines the intended form, materials and technique so the maker can identify structural, ergonomic and visual weaknesses before they are repeated across a production run.

options.label: D
options.text: It makes inspection of later units unnecessary once the first looks sound
options.rationale: Later units can vary through materials and workmanship, so production quality checks remain necessary after prototype approval.

questions.workedSolution: A prototype combines the intended form, materials and technique so the maker can identify structural, ergonomic and visual weaknesses before they are repeated across a production run. Therefore the correct answer is C: It tests dimensions, construction, appearance and fitness for purpose before repeated production.

questions.prompt: Why must a woven basket base be checked for shape and flatness before the sides are raised?

options.label: A
options.text: Postpone all base correction until after the rim locks the stakes
options.rationale: Once the walls and rim are complete, correcting base geometry becomes harder and may damage several finished courses.

options.label: B
options.text: Accept a rocking base as a deliberate sign of hand production
options.rationale: Hand production allows natural variation, but instability is a fitness defect when the basket is intended to stand securely.

options.label: C
options.text: Raise the sides first because their tension will flatten any twisted base
options.rationale: Side tension usually preserves or magnifies an uneven foundation instead of reliably flattening it.

options.label: D
options.text: Errors in the base will influence the alignment and stability of the whole form
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. The base establishes the stake spacing and footprint, so early correction prevents a persistent lean, rocking product or unequal wall circumference that becomes harder to remedy later.

questions.workedSolution: The base establishes the stake spacing and footprint, so early correction prevents a persistent lean, rocking product or unequal wall circumference that becomes harder to remedy later. Therefore the correct answer is D: Errors in the base will influence the alignment and stability of the whole form.

questions.prompt: What does upsetting the stakes mean during stake-and-strand construction?

options.label: A
options.text: Cut the base stakes flush before any wall weaving begins
options.rationale: Cutting the stakes removes the structural members needed to continue the basket walls above the base.

options.label: B
options.text: Complete and bind the rim before changing the direction of the stakes
options.rationale: The rim is made after the walls, so it cannot precede the upward turn that establishes those walls.

options.label: C
options.text: Bend the horizontal weavers upward while leaving all stakes flat
options.rationale: Weavers travel around the framework; changing wall direction requires the stakes themselves to rise from the base.

options.label: D
options.text: Bending the base stakes upward to establish the side walls
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. After the base reaches its planned size, the stakes are conditioned and turned upward in a controlled manner so weaving can continue around the emerging wall without splitting them.

questions.workedSolution: After the base reaches its planned size, the stakes are conditioned and turned upward in a controlled manner so weaving can continue around the emerging wall without splitting them. Therefore the correct answer is D: Bending the base stakes upward to establish the side walls.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes fitching from finishing in basketry?

options.label: A
options.text: Fitching is close one-strand randing used to fill the wall, while finishing means raising the stakes from the base
options.rationale: Close single-weaver randing fills the wall and raising stakes begins side construction; neither operation defines open-work fitching or final finishing.

options.label: B
options.text: Fitching forms a square-knot handle from cords, while finishing colours unsized materials before construction
options.rationale: A square-knot handle is macrame construction, and colouring is material preparation; neither describes fitching or the final refinement stage.

options.label: C
options.text: Fitching is planned open-work twining around stakes, while finishing secures, trims and refines the completed basket
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Fitching is an open-work weave commonly worked with two weavers in a twining or pairing action, with deliberate spaces between rows. Finishing is the later securing, trimming, smoothing and suitable surface treatment of the whole product.

options.label: D
options.text: Fitching locks the final border around cut stake ends, while finishing creates spaced open rows through the wall
options.rationale: This reverses the terms: a border secures stake ends during finishing, whereas fitching creates controlled open spacing within the woven structure.

questions.workedSolution: Fitching is an open-work weave commonly worked with two weavers in a twining or pairing action, with deliberate spaces between rows. Finishing is the later securing, trimming, smoothing and suitable surface treatment of the whole product. Therefore the correct answer is C: Fitching is planned open-work twining around stakes, while finishing secures, trims and refines the completed basket.

questions.prompt: Why should a carrying handle be anchored through several sound structural elements?

options.label: A
options.text: Fasten each handle end to a single thick stake selected mainly for its diameter
options.rationale: One thick stake still concentrates repeated lifting force at a single member and connection instead of sharing it through the basket structure.

options.label: B
options.text: Loop each end around the rim braid at opposite points because the border already spans the opening
options.rationale: The rim maintains the opening but may not carry the full service load unless the attachment also transfers force into reinforced wall stakes.

options.label: C
options.text: The load is distributed instead of concentrating at one weak strand
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Spreading the connection through stakes, rim members or reinforced areas lowers local stress and reduces the chance of pull-out when the loaded basket is lifted repeatedly.

options.label: D
options.text: Stitch each end through several nearby decorative weavers without engaging the main stakes
options.rationale: Several decorative weavers can spread stitches visually while remaining too lightly anchored to provide a reliable structural load path.

questions.workedSolution: Spreading the connection through stakes, rim members or reinforced areas lowers local stress and reduces the chance of pull-out when the loaded basket is lifted repeatedly. Therefore the correct answer is C: The load is distributed instead of concentrating at one weak strand.

questions.prompt: Which working sequence produces a basic over-two-under-two twill weave in basketry?

options.label: A
options.text: Pass each weaver over two stakes and under two, offsetting the next row to develop a diagonal progression
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. A basic twill groups crossings over two and under two and offsets successive rows, so the visible floats advance diagonally. The alternatives describe simple randing, open fitching and a multi-weaver strengthening course.

options.label: B
options.text: Pass one weaver over one stake and under one, continuing the same alternation around the basket
options.rationale: Over-one-under-one with a single weaver is simple randing; it lacks the grouped floats and staggered diagonal movement that identify this twill.

options.label: C
options.text: Work three weavers in sequence around the stakes so each course forms a firm horizontal band
options.rationale: A three-weaver strengthening course can form a firm band, but its sequential wrapping action is not the staggered two-over-two structure specified.

options.label: D
options.text: Twist two weavers around successive stakes and leave measured open spaces between the woven rows
options.rationale: Two weavers twisted around stakes with deliberate gaps describe fitching or open twining rather than an over-two-under-two twill progression.

questions.workedSolution: A basic twill groups crossings over two and under two and offsets successive rows, so the visible floats advance diagonally. The alternatives describe simple randing, open fitching and a multi-weaver strengthening course. Therefore the correct answer is A: Pass each weaver over two stakes and under two, offsetting the next row to develop a diagonal progression.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes an illustration from a sketch in basketry design development?

options.label: A
options.text: A sketch quickly explores an idea with limited detail, while an illustration develops form through clearer drawing, detail and shading
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. A sketch captures and tests an idea rapidly, often with few details. An illustration communicates the intended basket more fully through developed drawing, visible details and shading, so it can explain form more clearly to another viewer.

options.label: B
options.text: Sketch and illustration are interchangeable whenever both show the basket from a single viewpoint
options.rationale: Viewpoint alone does not make the terms equivalent; their degree of development and communication purpose remain materially different.

options.label: C
options.text: A sketch is the polished presentation image, while an illustration is an unrefined outline made before options are explored
options.rationale: This swaps their usual levels of development: the sketch is exploratory, while the illustration is prepared to communicate the selected idea clearly.

options.label: D
options.text: A sketch is the final measured construction drawing, while an illustration is the first loose record of an idea
options.rationale: A final measured drawing is a technical or working drawing, not the defining purpose of a quick exploratory sketch; the sequence is also reversed.

questions.workedSolution: A sketch captures and tests an idea rapidly, often with few details. An illustration communicates the intended basket more fully through developed drawing, visible details and shading, so it can explain form more clearly to another viewer. Therefore the correct answer is A: A sketch quickly explores an idea with limited detail, while an illustration develops form through clearer drawing, detail and shading.

questions.prompt: Which expense is most appropriately treated as workshop overhead rather than direct material for one basket?

options.label: A
options.text: The cane lengths measured and woven into that basket
options.rationale: Cane consumed by one identified product is traceable direct material rather than shared workshop overhead.

options.label: B
options.text: The dye quantity recorded specifically for that basket
options.rationale: A measured dye allocation used specifically for the unit can be charged directly to that basket.

options.label: C
options.text: A fair share of workshop lighting and rent
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Lighting and rent support several products and cannot normally be traced economically to one unit, so a consistent allocation method includes their share in total production cost.

options.label: D
options.text: The handle fittings permanently attached to that basket
options.rationale: Fittings incorporated into one finished item are direct inputs, unlike rent or lighting shared across production.

questions.workedSolution: Lighting and rent support several products and cannot normally be traced economically to one unit, so a consistent allocation method includes their share in total production cost. Therefore the correct answer is C: A fair share of workshop lighting and rent.

questions.prompt: What is the soundest basis for setting a sustainable selling price?

options.label: A
options.text: Copy the lowest competing price even when construction and quality differ
options.rationale: Competitor prices inform a market check, but differences in quality, size and cost prevent blind copying.

options.label: B
options.text: Ignore rejected trials and normal waste when estimating production cost
options.rationale: Reasonable process waste and trials consume resources and should be planned rather than hidden from the cost base.

options.label: C
options.text: Total cost plus a reasoned profit margin, checked against value and market conditions
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Pricing should recover materials, labour and allocated overhead before profit, while comparison with customer value and market conditions tests whether the offer is commercially realistic.

options.label: D
options.text: Recover direct material only and treat skilled labour as having no cost
options.rationale: A price that omits labour and overhead cannot reliably sustain production even if it replaces the consumed fibre.

questions.workedSolution: Pricing should recover materials, labour and allocated overhead before profit, while comparison with customer value and market conditions tests whether the offer is commercially realistic. Therefore the correct answer is C: Total cost plus a reasoned profit margin, checked against value and market conditions.

questions.prompt: Why is the sequence of operations written before producing several matching baskets?

options.label: A
options.text: It coordinates preparation, weaving and finishing while reducing delay and rework
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. A planned route groups suitable operations, identifies dependencies and quality checks, and makes time and material needs visible before repeated errors affect the full production run.

options.label: B
options.text: Inspect the completed batch after packaging rather than at intermediate stages
options.rationale: End-only inspection allows one process error to spread through the batch instead of being corrected at an early control point.

options.label: C
options.text: Apply the final finish before checking dimensions or structural joints
options.rationale: Premature finishing can conceal defects and must be redone if dimensions or joints require correction.

options.label: D
options.text: Prepare materials separately for each unit without a common specification
options.rationale: Ad hoc preparation increases variation; a common specification supports matching units and efficient batch work.

questions.workedSolution: A planned route groups suitable operations, identifies dependencies and quality checks, and makes time and material needs visible before repeated errors affect the full production run. Therefore the correct answer is A: It coordinates preparation, weaving and finishing while reducing delay and rework.

questions.prompt: Which portfolio entry best demonstrates development of an original basket design?

options.label: A
options.text: Annotated sketches, material trials, process photographs and evaluation of the result
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. A strong portfolio links intention to testing and outcome, showing how observations from samples and construction informed changes rather than displaying only an unexplained final object.

options.label: B
options.text: A downloaded basket image presented without identifying it as reference
options.rationale: Unattributed reference imagery does not establish authorship and may falsely imply that another maker’s work is the candidate’s process.

options.label: C
options.text: One final photograph without dimensions, trials or reflection
options.rationale: A final image records outcome but cannot demonstrate how the maker tested, changed and resolved the design.

options.label: D
options.text: A list of available tools that never connects them to design decisions
options.rationale: Tool names alone do not show why materials, construction or form changed during development.

questions.workedSolution: A strong portfolio links intention to testing and outcome, showing how observations from samples and construction informed changes rather than displaying only an unexplained final object. Therefore the correct answer is A: Annotated sketches, material trials, process photographs and evaluation of the result.

questions.prompt: Which inspection finding gives the strongest evidence of sound basketry workmanship?

options.label: A
options.text: A flexible rim that changes shape whenever the basket is lifted
options.rationale: A service rim should retain the opening and secure stakes; uncontrolled movement indicates inadequate construction.

options.label: B
options.text: Attractive colour that conceals irregular gaps and loose courses
options.rationale: Colour cannot compensate for openings or loose weave that reduce containment, durability and structural consistency.

options.label: C
options.text: Uneven tension accepted because all handmade work must be structurally irregular
options.rationale: Handmaking permits character, but unequal structural tension remains a correctable workmanship defect rather than a requirement.

options.label: D
options.text: Even tension, stable form, secure borders and no hazardous projecting ends
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Quality includes structure, fitness and safety as well as appearance, so regular tension, accurate form and securely finished ends provide evidence that the product can perform its intended service.

questions.workedSolution: Quality includes structure, fitness and safety as well as appearance, so regular tension, accurate form and securely finished ends provide evidence that the product can perform its intended service. Therefore the correct answer is D: Even tension, stable form, secure borders and no hazardous projecting ends.

questions.prompt: Why should a loose rim binding be repaired before the basket is used again?

options.label: A
options.text: Continued handling can release stakes and enlarge the structural failure
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. The rim restrains stake ends and receives frequent handling, so early repair restores confinement before repeated movement damages adjacent weaving or creates sharp exposed elements.

options.label: B
options.text: Add a fresh decorative binding over the loose course while leaving its failed ends unsecured
options.rationale: An overlay can conceal movement without restoring the failed mechanical path, so the original loose ends still need to be secured or replaced.

options.label: C
options.text: Trim the projecting fibres flush and rely on the remaining border until the next full maintenance
options.rationale: Trimming removes a visible symptom but not the loosened restraint, allowing movement to continue through the remaining border structure.

options.label: D
options.text: Moisten and retighten the visible wrap without checking whether hidden binding ends have broken
options.rationale: Retightening the surface may improve appearance, but an unexamined broken end can continue releasing the stake confinement beneath it.

questions.workedSolution: The rim restrains stake ends and receives frequent handling, so early repair restores confinement before repeated movement damages adjacent weaving or creates sharp exposed elements. Therefore the correct answer is A: Continued handling can release stakes and enlarge the structural failure.

questions.prompt: Which harvesting practice best supports a renewable supply of basketry cane?

options.label: A
options.text: Return each season to the most accessible patch and take only its straightest mature stems
options.rationale: Selecting only the best stems from one accessible patch year after year depletes that patch and leaves a progressively poorer material population.

options.label: B
options.text: Cut mature stems selectively while protecting regrowth and the habitat
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Selective harvesting retains regenerative capacity and habitat conditions, allowing future stems to mature while reducing erosion and resource depletion associated with complete clearance.

options.label: C
options.text: Retain the oldest declining stems permanently and harvest the vigorous mature stems around them
options.rationale: Declining stems do not substitute for healthy regeneration, while repeatedly removing vigorous mature growth reduces future productive structure.

options.label: D
options.text: Rotate between clumps while taking most market-size stems and soft young shoots from the selected clump
options.rationale: Rotation does not restore regeneration if a harvested clump loses both mature stock and the young shoots needed for its next growth cycle.

questions.workedSolution: Selective harvesting retains regenerative capacity and habitat conditions, allowing future stems to mature while reducing erosion and resource depletion associated with complete clearance. Therefore the correct answer is B: Cut mature stems selectively while protecting regrowth and the habitat.

questions.prompt: What is the best use of clean short offcuts that cannot serve as full-length weavers?

options.label: A
options.text: Combine all clean offcuts into mixed bundles for decoration without grading them by stiffness or length
options.rationale: Decoration still needs controlled material response and scale; ungraded stiffness and length make placement and repeated pattern unreliable.

options.label: B
options.text: Join short offcuts end to end with concealed overlaps so they can replace continuous structural weavers
options.rationale: Hidden end-to-end joints interrupt fibre continuity and may slip under load, so short pieces should not impersonate full structural weavers.

options.label: C
options.text: Sort them for samples, small bindings, decoration or other suitable components
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Sorting by length, condition and material lets safe offcuts substitute for new stock in appropriately small tasks, reducing waste without placing unsuitable pieces in critical structural positions.

options.label: D
options.text: Reserve the offcuts for future repairs without separating them by species, moisture condition or size
options.rationale: Repair stock must match the receiving work closely, so unsorted species, moisture and dimensions reduce rather than improve its future usefulness.

questions.workedSolution: Sorting by length, condition and material lets safe offcuts substitute for new stock in appropriately small tasks, reducing waste without placing unsuitable pieces in critical structural positions. Therefore the correct answer is C: Sort them for samples, small bindings, decoration or other suitable components.

questions.prompt: How should a newly completed carrying basket be checked for fitness for purpose?

options.label: A
options.text: Hang the intended load from the handle once and record only whether the attachment remains intact
options.rationale: A pass-or-fail handle check misses progressive loosening, wall distortion and base response that appear while the complete basket carries service load.

options.label: B
options.text: Press the base, walls and handle separately by hand instead of testing the assembled load path
options.rationale: Separate hand pressure does not reproduce the connected forces created by contents and lifting, so it cannot verify whole-product performance.

options.label: C
options.text: Apply a controlled representative load while observing the base, sides and handle attachments
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. A controlled service-relevant test verifies that the complete load path performs without excessive distortion or loosening, while avoiding the damage and poor evidence produced by uncontrolled overloading.

options.label: D
options.text: Inspect symmetry and weave tightness while empty, then infer capacity from the stated cane grade
options.rationale: Empty visual checks support quality control but cannot show how joints and woven members redistribute the intended load during carrying.

questions.workedSolution: A controlled service-relevant test verifies that the complete load path performs without excessive distortion or loosening, while avoiding the damage and poor evidence produced by uncontrolled overloading. Therefore the correct answer is C: Apply a controlled representative load while observing the base, sides and handle attachments.

questions.prompt: Which description best identifies kip in leather classification?

options.label: A
options.text: A goat skin selected mainly for its tight grain and small area
options.rationale: Goat skin is a separate species classification; its compact grain does not make it kip.

options.label: B
options.text: The lower flesh split removed from any heavy hide during splitting
options.rationale: A flesh split describes a layer produced by splitting, not the age and size class called kip.

options.label: C
options.text: A bovine hide from an animal older than a calf but lighter than a mature cow hide
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Kip occupies an intermediate bovine class between calfskin and mature cow hide, so its area, thickness and fibre character differ from both lighter calfskin and heavier cow hide.

options.label: D
options.text: A mature cow hide classified by its finished colour rather than age and weight
options.rationale: Mature cow hide is heavier stock, and colour grading does not redefine it as kip.

questions.workedSolution: Kip occupies an intermediate bovine class between calfskin and mature cow hide, so its area, thickness and fibre character differ from both lighter calfskin and heavier cow hide. Therefore the correct answer is C: A bovine hide from an animal older than a calf but lighter than a mature cow hide.

questions.prompt: How does split leather differ from grained leather made from the same hide?

options.label: A
options.text: Grained leather is commonly the flesh split after a surface pattern has been printed on it
options.rationale: A flesh split may be embossed to imitate grain, but genuine grained leather retains the outer layer.

options.label: B
options.text: Split leather retains much of the natural grain but is cut into smaller panels
options.rationale: Panel size is unrelated to layer identity; cutting a grain layer smaller does not make it a split.

options.label: C
options.text: Split and grained leather describe identical layers but different dye colours
options.rationale: The terms identify structural layers and surfaces, not alternative names for colour treatments.

options.label: D
options.text: Split leather comes from a lower layer and lacks the original natural grain surface
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Mechanical splitting separates hide layers: the grain layer retains the natural outer surface, while a lower split can be finished or embossed but does not possess that original grain.

questions.workedSolution: Mechanical splitting separates hide layers: the grain layer retains the natural outer surface, while a lower split can be finished or embossed but does not possess that original grain. Therefore the correct answer is D: Split leather comes from a lower layer and lacks the original natural grain surface.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of buffing leather during surface preparation?

options.label: A
options.text: Apply pigment mechanically while leaving the surface texture unchanged
options.rationale: Pigment coating adds colour and coverage after preparation; it is not the abrasive buffing step.

options.label: B
options.text: Remove thickness evenly through the whole hide in the same way as splitting
options.rationale: Splitting separates layers and controls bulk thickness; buffing treats only a surface zone.

options.label: C
options.text: Compress the grain with a glazing tool until it becomes a firm polished surface
options.rationale: Glazing compresses and polishes a surface, whereas buffing cuts it lightly with abrasive material.

options.label: D
options.text: Use controlled abrasion to level defects or raise a uniform nap for the intended finish
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Buffing uses an abrasive action on the grain or flesh side to reduce surface irregularities or develop a controlled nap, depending on whether corrected grain, nubuck or suede is required.

questions.workedSolution: Buffing uses an abrasive action on the grain or flesh side to reduce surface irregularities or develop a controlled nap, depending on whether corrected grain, nubuck or suede is required. Therefore the correct answer is D: Use controlled abrasion to level defects or raise a uniform nap for the intended finish.

questions.prompt: What fundamental change does tanning produce in a prepared pelt?

options.label: A
options.text: It removes hair by alkaline swelling without stabilising the collagen
options.rationale: Liming helps unhair and open fibres, yet an untanned limed pelt remains perishable.

options.label: B
options.text: It stabilises collagen against putrefaction and excessive water sensitivity
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Tanning agents create stabilising interactions in the collagen structure, converting a perishable pelt into leather with improved biological, wet and thermal stability.

options.label: C
options.text: It preserves the raw pelt temporarily by drawing out moisture with salt
options.rationale: Salting delays bacterial damage before processing but does not create permanently tanned collagen.

options.label: D
options.text: It lubricates already tanned fibres so the dried leather remains flexible
options.rationale: Fatliquoring improves flexibility after tannage; it does not perform the collagen stabilisation itself.

questions.workedSolution: Tanning agents create stabilising interactions in the collagen structure, converting a perishable pelt into leather with improved biological, wet and thermal stability. Therefore the correct answer is B: It stabilises collagen against putrefaction and excessive water sensitivity.

questions.prompt: Why should leather thickness and stretch be checked in several zones before laying out a bag pattern?

options.label: A
options.text: A single centre reading is sufficient to represent the mechanical behaviour of the hide
options.rationale: The centre may be firmer than edge zones, so one reading cannot represent the complete hide.

options.label: B
options.text: Natural variation determines which zones suit straps, gussets and broad panels
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. A hide varies from firm backbone areas to stretchier belly and flank zones, so measuring and flexing several areas helps assign each component to material that suits its load and form.

options.label: C
options.text: Stretch direction matters for garment leather but not for loaded straps or handles
options.rationale: Loaded components are especially sensitive to stretch direction because elongation changes fit and durability.

options.label: D
options.text: Matching surface colour indicates equal substance and firmness across the zones
options.rationale: Colour can appear uniform over zones that still differ materially in thickness, stretch and fibre density.

questions.workedSolution: A hide varies from firm backbone areas to stretchier belly and flank zones, so measuring and flexing several areas helps assign each component to material that suits its load and form. Therefore the correct answer is B: Natural variation determines which zones suit straps, gussets and broad panels.

questions.prompt: Which description correctly identifies combination tanning?

options.label: A
options.text: Fresh hides are wet salted and later brined, with the two preservation steps counted as separate tannages
options.rationale: Wet salting and brining are raw-hide preservation methods; using both does not create two collagen-stabilising tannages.

options.label: B
options.text: Finished leather is bleached and then dyed, combining two colour treatments into a tannage
options.rationale: Bleaching and dyeing alter colour, but neither treatment supplies the second collagen-stabilising tannage required here.

options.label: C
options.text: A pickled pelt receives one chrome-tanning bath followed by neutralisation and drying
options.rationale: Pickling prepares a pelt for chrome penetration, while neutralisation and drying do not add a second tanning system.

options.label: D
options.text: The leather receives two compatible tannages in sequence so their properties complement one another
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Combination tanning deliberately applies two compatible tanning systems, such as vegetable tannage followed by chrome or another mineral tannage, to combine useful handle, colour, strength or ageing properties.

questions.workedSolution: Combination tanning deliberately applies two compatible tanning systems, such as vegetable tannage followed by chrome or another mineral tannage, to combine useful handle, colour, strength or ageing properties. Therefore the correct answer is D: The leather receives two compatible tannages in sequence so their properties complement one another.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of fleshing before tanning?

options.label: A
options.text: Introduce lubricating oils between fibres before drying
options.rationale: Fibre lubrication is fatliquoring after tannage, not removal of tissue from a raw pelt.

options.label: B
options.text: Abrade the grain lightly so pigment can cover natural marks
options.rationale: Light grain abrasion is buffing, a later surface operation with a different purpose.

options.label: C
options.text: Remove adhering fat, connective tissue and flesh from the inner surface
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Fleshing clears residual tissue that would decay or obstruct even chemical penetration, leaving a cleaner pelt for subsequent beamhouse and tanning operations.

options.label: D

questions.prompt: What does burnishing do to a properly prepared vegetable-tanned leather edge?

options.label: A
options.text: It compacts and smooths exposed fibres using controlled moisture or compound and friction
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. After levelling and bevelling, controlled friction aligns and compacts edge fibres into a smoother surface that is comfortable and more resistant to light abrasion.

options.label: B
options.text: It deposits enough adhesive to become the main structural joint
options.rationale: Burnishing compounds assist surface smoothing; they are not structural joining adhesives.

options.label: C
options.text: It raises a loose nap so the edge resembles the flesh side of suede
options.rationale: Raising a nap is associated with abrasive suede preparation, the opposite of edge compaction.

options.label: D
options.text: It removes a broad taper from the edge to reduce folded thickness

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes scorching from stippling on leather?

options.label: A
options.text: Scorching builds dotted texture with a pointed punch, while stippling browns the grain with a heated tool
options.rationale: This swaps the methods: a pointed tool can stipple repeated marks, while controlled heat produces the scorched tonal line or area.

options.label: B
options.text: Scorching uses controlled heat to darken a design, while stippling forms tone or texture with repeated small dots or impressions
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Scorching, or pyrographic work, controls a heated tool to brown the leather without burning through it; stippling accumulates separate dots or impressions to create texture, shading or emphasis.

options.label: C
options.text: Scorching secures cut motifs to a ground, while stippling recesses a contrasting insert flush with the surface
options.rationale: Attaching cut motifs is appliqué and fitting a flush contrasting insert is inlay; neither operation defines scorching or stippling.

options.label: D
options.text: Scorching removes a thin surface layer with a knife, while stippling applies a continuous opaque dye film
options.rationale: Knife removal describes carving or surface cutting, while an opaque dye film is colouring rather than a field of stippled impressions.

questions.workedSolution: Scorching, or pyrographic work, controls a heated tool to brown the leather without burning through it; stippling accumulates separate dots or impressions to create texture, shading or emphasis. Therefore the correct answer is B: Scorching uses controlled heat to darken a design, while stippling forms tone or texture with repeated small dots or impressions.

questions.prompt: Which workshop expense is normally treated as a fixed cost when costing a batch of leather belts?

options.label: A
options.text: Leather consumed by each belt pattern
options.rationale: Leather consumption varies with the number, size and yield of belts, making it a variable material cost.

options.label: B
options.text: Buckles purchased for the number of belts made

options.label: C
options.text: Monthly rent for the production space
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Rent is incurred for the period even if output changes, while leather, buckles and unit packaging generally rise or fall with the number of belts produced.

options.label: D
options.text: Packaging used for each completed belt

questions.prompt: How should variable cost per leather wallet be estimated for a planned production run?

options.label: A
options.text: Divide monthly rent alone by the selling price of one wallet
options.rationale: Rent is a fixed overhead and dividing it by selling price does not measure variable consumption.

options.label: B
options.text: Subtract direct materials from revenue and call the balance variable cost
options.rationale: Revenue minus materials is a margin measure and omits other variable inputs such as hardware and packaging.

options.label: C
options.text: Add leather, lining, thread, hardware and unit packaging consumed by one wallet
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Variable unit cost follows the resources consumed by each wallet; fixed overhead and durable equipment are allocated separately when calculating total cost and price.

options.label: D

options.rationale: Durable tools serve many units and should be depreciated or allocated rather than charged fully to one wallet.

questions.prompt: Which marketing action best tests demand for a new handmade leather-bag design in Ghana?

options.label: A
options.text: Show a priced prototype to a defined customer segment and record orders, objections and preferred features
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. A priced prototype tested with intended buyers produces evidence about willingness to pay, use needs and objections before scarce leather and labour are committed to inventory.

options.label: B
options.text: Ask workshop staff to judge the colour and shape before setting the production quantity
options.rationale: Workshop opinions do not substitute for feedback from the customer group expected to purchase and use it.

options.label: C

options.rationale: Large speculative production increases stock risk before demand and feature preferences are known.

options.label: D

options.rationale: A photograph lacks the cost, quality and specification detail needed for defensible price comparison.

questions.prompt: Which response best addresses common leather-enterprise constraints in Ghana such as imported inputs, humid storage and inconsistent material supply?

options.label: A
options.text: Hold damp leather in sealed stacks to protect it from dust during the humid season
options.rationale: Sealed damp stacks trap the moisture that supports mould, staining and fibre deterioration.

options.label: B
options.text: Qualify multiple suppliers, inspect incoming leather, control dry ventilated storage and price from current landed costs
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Supplier diversification, incoming quality checks, moisture control and current cost records reduce disruption, mould loss and margin erosion when local availability and imported-input costs vary.

questions.prompt: What combined check best supports quality and care before a leather bag is delivered?

options.label: A
options.text: Inspect seams, edges and hardware under load, then give care advice suited to the leather and finish
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Delivery inspection should confirm structural and finish performance, while material-specific advice on cleaning, moisture, heat and conditioning helps the customer preserve the article safely.

options.label: B
options.text: Inspect the lining appearance and defer structural testing until a sample is used
options.rationale: Lining appearance does not reveal seam strength, edge security, handle anchorage or faulty hardware.

options.label: C
options.text: Apply a heavy conditioner before conducting a colourfastness test
options.rationale: Conditioners can darken or disrupt finishes, so compatibility and colourfastness must be tested first.

options.label: D
options.text: Judge quality from surface shine and advise frequent soaking to maintain flexibility
options.rationale: Shine can hide weak construction, and soaking risks distortion, dye movement and loss of fibre lubrication.

questions.workedSolution: Delivery inspection should confirm structural and finish performance, while material-specific advice on cleaning, moisture, heat and conditioning helps the customer preserve the article safely. Therefore the correct answer is A: Inspect seams, edges and hardware under load, then give care advice suited to the leather and finish.
